name: o2n
description: Migrate an Obsidian vault into Notion from a conversation: keeps folders, wikilinks, frontmatter, Dataview fields and attachments, with a dry run first and resumable runs.

allowed_vaults.title: Allowed vault paths
allowed_vaults.description: Absolute path of each Obsidian vault o2n may read, separated by commas. o2n refuses every other folder. Leave empty to use vaults saved with `npx @tk_wfl/o2n-cli mcp allow`.

notion_token.title: Notion token
notion_token.description: A Notion personal access token (recommended) or internal integration token. Leave empty to use a token saved with `npx @tk_wfl/o2n-cli login --token`.

enable_write.title: Allow writing to Notion
enable_write.description: Off: o2n only scans, plans and runs dry runs, unless you turned writing on with `npx @tk_wfl/o2n-cli mcp write on`. On: a real migration can create pages in Notion, and only after Claude passes the confirmation phrase.

write_confirmation_token.title: Confirmation phrase
write_confirmation_token.description: At least 16 characters. A real migration starts only when Claude passes this exact phrase, so tell it to Claude in chat only when you want the migration to run. Leave empty to use the phrase saved with `npx @tk_wfl/o2n-cli mcp write on`.

requests_per_second.title: Notion requests per second
requests_per_second.description: 1 to 10. Keep 2 or 3 on Notion Free and Plus. Business and Enterprise allow up to 10, which makes large migrations faster.
